descriptionChirho: Outcome of wise conduct: to prosper or have success, confirmed by Arabic نجح (najaha) / أفلح (aflaha) = succeed, Korean 형통하다/성공하다, Swahili -fanikiwa, Hindi सफल, Spanish prosperar/tener éxito; includes contexts where 'acting wisely' is rendered as 'succeeding' in Arabic

Attributive or stative: to be prudent, wise, or discerning in character; Arabic فَطِنٌ (discerning) / فَهيمٌ (wise), Korean 슬기로운/지혜로운 (wise), Swahili mwenye busara (one with prudence), Hindi समझदार/बुद्धिमान; includes imperative 'be wise' and cohortative 'I will give heed'

Cognitive act of understanding or grasping meaning; Arabic فَهِمَ (fahima = understand) / فَهْم (understanding), Korean 깨닫다 (realize/understand), Swahili -elewa/-fahamu (understand), Hindi समझना (to understand), Spanish entender; covers finite verbs, infinitives, and nominal infinitive forms meaning 'understanding'

Substantivized participle denoting a class of wise or discerning people; Arabic الْحُكَمَاءُ (the wise) / الْفَاهِمِينَ (the understanding ones) / الْمَاهِرِينَ (the skilled), Korean 지혜로운 자들 (wise ones), Swahili wenye hekima (those with wisdom); used with article or conjunction as a group designation

Causative: to teach, instruct, or cause someone to understand; Arabic عَلَّمَ (teach) / أَفْهَمَ (make understand) / أُفَهِّمَ (cause to comprehend), Korean 가르치다 (teach) / 깨닫게 하다 (cause to realize), Swahili -fundisha (teach), Hindi सिखाना (to teach) / समझाना (to explain); the true Hifil causative meaning distinct from stative or cognitive senses

To consider carefully, pay close attention to, or observe with discernment; Arabic تَأَمَّلَ (contemplate) / تَفَطَّنَ (be perceptive/notice), Korean 살피다 (examine) / 주의하다 (pay attention), Swahili -angalia (look at) / -fikiri (think about), Hindi ध्यान देना (pay attention); distinct from mere understanding by its emphasis on attentive observation

Possessing practical skill or expertise in a craft or domain; Arabic مَاهِرٍ (skilled/expert), Korean 숙련된 (trained/practiced), Swahili hodari (capable/skilled), Hindi निपुण (proficient), Spanish hábil (able/skillful); denotes competence rather than moral wisdom or intellectual understanding

Technical musical or liturgical term used in psalm superscriptions; Arabic بِ فِطْنَةٍ (with discernment), Korean 교훈시 (didactic psalm), Swahili maskili (loanword); a nominal form whose exact meaning is debated but traditionally understood as a contemplative or instructive psalm type
